YNAB to Money Manager

Convert a YNAB transaction export into a clean file ready for Money Manager.

1

Add your YNAB transactions

Waiting for a file
What you need

Choose a transaction-level CSV or TSV from YNAB. This tool will convert the selected dates into a file you can import into Money Manager. The other two files are optional helpers.

Where to get these export files

YNAB transactions

  1. Open YNAB on a computer and select Reflect → Spending Breakdown.
  2. Choose the accounts, categories and date range, then select Export twice.
  3. Upload the downloaded file whose name ends in -transactions.csv or .tsv.

The other Spending Breakdown file contains totals and is not the transaction source.

Read YNAB’s export guide ↗

Income and Money Manager references

  • For an income check, export Reflect → Income v Expense from YNAB.
  • From Money Manager, use Export data to Excel. Choose data that includes every account and category you intend to map.
  • This Money Manager file only supplies exact names; you can also enter missing names in Settings.
Money Manager backup guide ↗

Dates to includeOnly YNAB transactions between these two dates will be added to the Money Manager import.

The start date must be on or before the end date.

How to finish

TSV

Money Manager import

UTF-8 tab-separated file with exact mapped names and sub-currency columns.

Test import

Download up to five ready rows before importing the full range.

How to import the file into Money Manager
  1. 1
    Back up Money Manager first

    Create a current backup before importing or deleting any test rows.

  2. 2
    Prepare Money Manager

    Create the mapped accounts and categories in the app first. If the file uses sub-currencies, add them under More → Configuration → Sub Currency Setting.

  3. 3
    Connect your phone to the computer

    In Finder on a current Mac, or iTunes on Windows/older macOS, open file sharing for Money Manager and copy import.tsv into MoneyManager/import.

  4. 4
    Import on the phone

    Open Money Manager → More → Backup, select import.tsv, and confirm the import.

  5. 5
    Test before the full import

    Import the five-row test first. Check the result, delete those test rows, then import the complete file.
